key_insight: Coupling parametric finite elements with symplectic Runge–Kutta time stepping preserves enclosed curve area exactly without additional constraints or auxiliary variables.
engineering_relevance: The method supports accurate simulation of surface-diffusion-driven interface evolution where conserving enclosed area is essential.
method: Discretize the classical BGN formulation with parametric finite elements.
Use q-stage Gauss Runge–Kutta schemes for temporal order 2q and unconditional area conservation.
Solve the fully implicit nonlinear system using an equivalent discrete formulation and monolithic damped Newton iteration.
evidence_signal: Tests on various evolving curves confirm exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, with Newton iterations rapidly dropping below 8 per step.
watch_item: Fully implicit, strongly nonlinear solves add implementation complexity; the abstract proves area conservation but does not establish unconditional discrete perimeter decrease.
paper_title: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
